subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, literal phrase (ordinal number of characters not specified)
notes: cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 'the implementor defines the ordinal number within the character code set being specified for each character within the native character set that is not specified by the literal-1 phrase' -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) (k 4.). Read CollatingModel.CodedCharacterSet.CharAt (ordinal <= NextFree -> RepByPos; else the want-th unspecified code unit in native order) and OrdinalCount (65536 for a literal-phrase set). Probe probe/p186/k4.cob at --std 85 and 2023: S1=Z S2=Y S3=X S4=00 S5=01 S70=B; CLASS 1 THRU 3 IN AL excludes W (native contiguous X..Z, GR12) — consistent. kb/Work/PB1092 (open, process_only, claims DOC-A.1-186) owes exactly this row; integrator must also correct docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 27's sentence 'GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it' (PB1092's second deliverable). No spec-derived test pins the scheme. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1092.
